question: Which book has been authored by Shovana Narayan and Geetika Kalha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian Mythology through Classical Dance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The book "Indian Mythology through Classical Dance" has been co-authored by the renowned Kathak exponent Shovana Narayan and Geetika Kalha. (शोवना नारायण एवं गीतिका कालरा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Shovana Narayan is a celebrated Kathak dancer, a recipient of the Padma Shri and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

• She is also a former Indian Audit and Accounts Service (IA&AS) officer.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms of India are Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya. Kathak originated in North India (Uttar Pradesh).

question: The rock-cut caves in Karnataka, mainly at Badami and Aihole, were built under the patronage of the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chalukyas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The rock-cut caves at Badami and Aihole in Karnataka were built under the patronage of the Chalukyas (of Badami/Vatapi). (चालुक्य वंश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Badami Chalukyas ruled from the 6th to 8th century CE with their capital at Badami (Vatapi); a famous ruler was Pulakeshin II, who defeated Harshavardhana.

• Aihole is often called the "cradle of Indian temple architecture", and Pattadakal (also Chalukyan) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• The Chalukya style blended the Nagara (North Indian) and Dravida (South Indian) temple styles, sometimes called the Vesara style.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India directs the State to provide public assistance to its citizens in case of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement, within the limits of its economic capacity and development?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 41.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 41 directs the State to make effective provision for securing the right to work, to education and to public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement, within the limits of its economic capacity. (अनुच्छेद 41)

• It is a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 12 — defines the term "State".

• Article 20 — protection in respect of conviction for offences.

• Article 32 — right to constitutional remedies (called the "heart and soul" of the Constitution by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar).

NOTE

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36–51) are contained in Part IV and were borrowed from the Irish Constitution. They are non-justiciable but fundamental in governance.

question:
Which of the following statements about the Ozone layer are true?

Statement A: It is found in the stratosphere.
Statement B: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are responsible for ozone hole.
Statement C: Ozone layer is found around 15-30 km above the earth's surface.
Statement D: Ozone layer is expected not to recover anymore now.
option_3: Only statements A, B and C
option_4: Only statement B, C and D
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only statements A, B and C.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement A is true — the ozone layer lies in the stratosphere.

• Statement B is true — Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are the main cause of the ozone hole.

• Statement C is true — the ozone layer is found roughly 15-30 km above the Earth's surface.

• Statement D is false — the ozone layer is actually expected to recover over the coming decades thanks to the Montreal Protocol.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The ozone layer (O₃) absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the Sun, protecting life on Earth.

• The Montreal Protocol (1987) phased out ozone-depleting substances like CFCs; 16 September is observed as the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer.

NOTE

• Layers of the atmosphere (bottom to top): Troposphere, Stratosphere (ozone layer), Mesosphere, Thermosphere, Exosphere.

question: In which of the following sessions of Congress did the Party issue a call to celebrate 26th January as 'Purna Swaraj Day'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lahore 1929.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the Lahore Session of the Congress (1929), presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, the resolution of Purna Swaraj (Complete Independence) was passed, and a call was given to celebrate 26th January 1930 as "Purna Swaraj Day / Independence Day". (लाहौर अधिवेशन 1929)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• At Lahore, the tricolour flag of freedom was hoisted on the banks of the River Ravi.

• Because of this, when the Constitution came into force, 26th January 1950 was chosen as Republic Day.

NOTE

• Key sessions: 1885 Bombay (first, W.C. Bonnerjee), 1907 Surat (split), 1929 Lahore (Purna Swaraj), 1931 Karachi (Fundamental Rights resolution).

question: Padma Subrahmanyam is associated with which dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Padma Subrahmanyam is a legendary Indian classical dancer associated with the Bharatanatyam dance form; she is also a research scholar who developed the "Bharata Nrityam" style. (पद्मा सुब्रह्मण्यम — भरतनाट्यम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of sage Bharata.

• Padma Subrahmanyam has been honoured with the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan.

NOTE

• Famous Bharatanatyam exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Vyjayanthimala and Padma Subrahmanyam.

question: In 2023, Government of India has announced to set up a/an ______________ DigiLocker for use by MSMEs, large businesses and charitable trusts to store and share documents online securely.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Entity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Union Budget 2023-24, the government announced setting up an "Entity DigiLocker" for use by MSMEs, large businesses and charitable trusts to store and share documents securely online. (एंटिटी डिजिलॉकर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• DigiLocker is a flagship initiative under the Digital India programme, providing a cloud-based platform for storing and verifying documents.

• The Entity DigiLocker extends this facility from individuals to organisations/business entities.

NOTE

• The Union Budget 2023-24 (presented by Nirmala Sitharaman) had seven priorities called "Saptarishi", including inclusive development and unleashing the potential of businesses.

question: Oak and chestnut trees are found in which type of forest in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Montane forests.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Oak and chestnut trees are found in the Montane (mountain) forests of India, specifically in the temperate zone of the Himalayas (between about 1,000-2,000 m). (पर्वतीय वन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Montane forests change with altitude: wet temperate forests (oak, chestnut), then coniferous forests (pine, deodar, silver fir), and finally alpine forests and grasslands at higher altitudes.

• Mangrove forests grow in coastal, tidal areas (e.g., the Sundarbans); thorn forests are found in semi-arid regions like Rajasthan.

NOTE

• Major forest types in India: Tropical evergreen, Tropical deciduous (monsoon), Thorn, Montane (mountain) and Mangrove (tidal/littoral) forests.

question: Which of the following types of volcanic eruptions of Earth's volcanoes are most explosive?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Caldera.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Caldera" eruptions are the most explosive of all volcanic eruptions. They are so violent that the volcano collapses into itself, forming a large depression (a caldera). (कैल्डेरा — सबसे विस्फोटक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A caldera is a large, cauldron-like hollow that forms after the emptying of a magma chamber.

• Flood basalt provinces involve highly fluid lava spreading over large areas (e.g., the Deccan Traps), and are the least explosive.

NOTE

• Volcanic intrusive features: Batholith, Laccolith, Lapolith (lopolith), Phacolith, Sill and Dyke. Volcanoes are classified as active, dormant and extinct.

question: What is the term 'ace' commonly associated within sports?
option_2: A high jump technique in athletics
solution_text:
The correct answer is A fast serve in tennis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In sports, the term "ace" is commonly associated with tennis, where it refers to a serve that the opponent fails to touch, winning the point outright. (टेनिस में ऐस)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• An "ace" is a legal serve that lands in the correct service box and is not touched by the receiver.

• In volleyball, "ace" also means a serve that directly wins a point.

NOTE

• Tennis terms: love (0), deuce (40-40), advantage, fault, double fault, ace, break point, tie-break. The four Grand Slams are the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open.

question: Lokrang, a five-day festival organised by the Madhya Pradesh Adivasi Lok Kala Academy, begins on ________________ every year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 26th January.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lokrang", a five-day cultural festival organised by the Madhya Pradesh Adivasi Lok Kala Academy, begins every year on 26th January (Republic Day) at Bhopal. (लोकरंग महोत्सव — 26 जनवरी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The festival showcases tribal and folk art, dance, music and crafts from across India.

• It is held at Ravindra Bhavan / Bharat Bhavan area in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh.

NOTE

• Madhya Pradesh, the "Heart of India", is rich in tribal culture; other famous events include the Khajuraho Dance Festival and the Tansen Music Festival (Gwalior).

question: The Kakrapar Atomic Power Plant is located in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kakrapar Atomic Power Station (KAPS) is located in the Surat district of Gujarat, on the banks of the Tapi (Tapti) river. (काकरापार परमाणु ऊर्जा संयंत्र — गुजरात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kakrapar's Unit-3 (700 MW) was India's first indigenously designed Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) of this capacity.

• It is operated by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL).

NOTE

• Other nuclear plants: Tarapur (Maharashtra), Rawatbhata (Rajasthan), Kudankulam & Kalpakkam (Tamil Nadu), Narora (UP), Kaiga (Karnataka).

question: Vani Jairam, who won Padma Bhushan 2023, belongs to which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary playback singer Vani Jairam, awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2023, belonged to Tamil Nadu (born in Vellore). (वाणी जयराम — तमिलनाडु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Known as the "Meera of Modern India", she sang in many languages and won the National Film Award for Best Female Playback Singer three times.

• The Padma Bhushan is India's third-highest civilian award (after the Bharat Ratna and Padma Vibhushan).

NOTE

• Civilian awards order: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri. They were instituted in 1954.

question: A four-carbon chain with a triple bond is called _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is butyne.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A four-carbon chain with a triple bond is called "butyne" (an alkyne). The prefix "but-" denotes four carbons, and the suffix "-yne" denotes a carbon-carbon triple bond. (ब्यूटाइन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Butene (-ene) is a 4-carbon chain with a double bond (alkene).

• Butanal (-al) is a 4-carbon aldehyde; Butanol (-ol) is a 4-carbon alcohol.

NOTE

• Naming by carbon number: meth- (1), eth- (2), prop- (3), but- (4), pent- (5). Suffixes: -ane (single bond/alkane), -ene (double bond/alkene), -yne (triple bond/alkyne).

question: At the time of its adoption, the Constitution contained 395 Articles and ________ Schedules.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the time of its adoption (26 November 1949), the Constitution of India contained 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules. (मूल संविधान में 8 अनुसूचियाँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• At present, the Constitution has about 470 Articles, 25 Parts and 12 Schedules (after various amendments).

• The 9th Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment (1951), the 10th by the 52nd Amendment (1985), the 11th by the 73rd Amendment (1992) and the 12th by the 74th Amendment (1992).

NOTE

• The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day) and came into force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).

question:
A factory set up in my area is causing huge deforestation. Which of the following can we expect to see in the near future?

A) Lowering of ground water
B) Lower temperatures
C) Frequent rain
D) Arrival of new animals
solution_text:
The correct answer is A (Lowering of ground water).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Deforestation reduces the ability of the soil to absorb and retain water, which leads to lowering of the ground water table. Trees help in groundwater recharge; removing them increases runoff and depletes groundwater. (भूजल स्तर का गिरना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3 (which corresponds to statement A).

Additional Information

• Deforestation generally causes higher temperatures (not lower), less frequent rainfall (not more), and loss/migration of animals (not arrival of new ones).

• Forests maintain the water cycle, prevent soil erosion and act as carbon sinks.

NOTE

• Effects of deforestation: global warming, soil erosion, floods and droughts, loss of biodiversity and falling groundwater levels.

question: According to Article 280 of the Indian Constitution, the Finance Commission needs to be appointed for every ________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is five years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 280, the President constitutes a Finance Commission every fifth year (or earlier if required). It recommends the distribution of tax revenues between the Centre and the States. (वित्त आयोग — हर पाँच वर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial body with a chairman and four other members.

• The First Finance Commission (1951) was chaired by K. C. Neogy; the 16th Finance Commission is chaired by Arvind Panagariya.

NOTE

• The Finance Commission recommends: (i) distribution of net tax proceeds between Centre and States (vertical) and among States (horizontal), and (ii) grants-in-aid to States.

question: The last Mughal emperor of India was:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bahadur Shah II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bahadur Shah II (also known as Bahadur Shah Zafar) was the last Mughal emperor of India. He was declared the symbolic leader during the Revolt of 1857 and later exiled by the British to Rangoon (Burma), where he died in 1862. (बहादुर शाह ज़फ़र — अंतिम मुग़ल सम्राट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• He was a noted Urdu poet who wrote under the pen name "Zafar".

• After the 1857 revolt was crushed, the British formally ended Mughal rule and put India under the direct control of the British Crown (1858).

NOTE

• Major Mughal emperors: Babur (1526) → Humayun → Akbar → Jahangir → Shah Jahan → Aurangzeb → ... → Bahadur Shah Zafar (last).

question: At the ____________, Neeraj Chopra became the first Indian to win a gold medal in javelin throw.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asian Games, 2018.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the Asian Games 2018 (Jakarta, Indonesia), Neeraj Chopra became the first Indian to win a gold medal in javelin throw, with a throw of 88.06 m. (नीरज चोपड़ा — एशियाई खेल 2018)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Neeraj Chopra later won gold at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021), becoming India's first Olympic athletics gold medallist.

• He also won gold at the 2023 World Athletics Championships and gold again at the 2023 Asian Games (Hangzhou).

NOTE

• Neeraj Chopra is often called the "Golden Boy" of Indian athletics; his javelin coaches have included Uwe Hohn and Klaus Bartonietz.

question: A famous organisation Self-Employed Women's Association (SEWA) is related with which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Self-Employed Women's Association (SEWA) was founded in 1972 in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, by Ela Bhatt. It is a trade union of poor, self-employed women workers. (सेवा — गुजरात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Ela Bhatt, the founder of SEWA, was a Gandhian and a recipient of the Padma Bhushan and the Ramon Magsaysay Award.

• SEWA works to make women self-reliant through employment, income and social security.

NOTE

• SEWA also runs a cooperative SEWA Bank to provide banking and microfinance services to poor women workers.

question: How many Pillar Edicts or Major Pillar Edicts (PEs) of Ashoka are found?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seven.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• There are seven Major Pillar Edicts of Emperor Ashoka, inscribed on polished sandstone pillars. (अशोक के सात प्रमुख स्तंभ अभिलेख)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ashoka's edicts were mainly written in the Prakrit language and Brahmi script.

• Ashoka also has 14 Major Rock Edicts. His edicts were first deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837.

NOTE

• The Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath is India's National Emblem, and the wheel on it (Dharma Chakra) is on the National Flag. Ashoka belonged to the Mauryan dynasty.

question: In which year was the first Socio Economic and Caste Census (SECC) conducted in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2011.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first Socio Economic and Caste Census (SECC) in independent India was conducted in 2011. It aimed to collect data on the socio-economic status and caste of households. (सामाजिक-आर्थिक एवं जाति जनगणना — 2011)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The SECC 2011 is used to identify beneficiaries for various government welfare schemes.

• The last caste-based census before independence was in 1931.

NOTE

• The regular decadal Census of India first began in a synchronous manner in 1881 under W. C. Plowden; the census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General of India.

question: In May 2023, who was sworn in as Central Vigilance Commissioner?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Praveen Kumar Srivastava.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In May 2023, Praveen Kumar Srivastava was sworn in as the Central Vigilance Commissioner (CVC) of India. (प्रवीण कुमार श्रीवास्तव — केंद्रीय सतर्कता आयुक्त)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) is the apex body for tackling corruption in government offices; it was set up in 1964 on the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee.

• It was given statutory status by the CVC Act, 2003. It consists of a Central Vigilance Commissioner and up to two Vigilance Commissioners.

NOTE

• The CVC and Vigilance Commissioners are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee headed by the Prime Minister.

question: Who among the following is the author of the book, 'A History of British India'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is James Mill.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The book "The History of British India" (often referred to as "A History of British India") was written by the Scottish historian and economist James Mill (published in 1817). (जेम्स मिल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• James Mill controversially divided Indian history into three periods — Hindu, Muslim and British, a periodisation now widely criticised as biased.

• Grenville Austin wrote "The Indian Constitution: Cornerstone of a Nation".

NOTE

• James Mill was a proponent of utilitarianism (associated with Jeremy Bentham); his son John Stuart Mill was also a famous philosopher and economist.

question: Bharatanatyam dancer ________ received the Natya Kala Sarathy award from Sri Parthasarathy Swami Sabha in 2023 at Chennai.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Srekala Bharath.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bharatanatyam dancer Srekala Bharath received the "Natya Kala Sarathy" award from the Sri Parthasarathy Swami Sabha in 2023 at Chennai. (श्रेकला भरत — नाट्य कला सारथी पुरस्कार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, one of India's eight recognised classical dances.

• The Sri Parthasarathy Swami Sabha is a well-known cultural organisation in Chennai that promotes classical arts.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).
